page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the x86_64 architecture using the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The memory allocation is exceptionally dense, providing 1024.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a 7559 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3787.49 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2884.0. Multi-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 22126.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 58692.46, though multi-core stress-ng results fall into the average tier. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are highly efficient, with gzip compression reaching 41.3 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, measuring 101.48 GB/sec for read-only operations.

While the instance excels at single-core execution and memory-intensive operations, it exhibits limitations in large-scale AI workloads, with large model LLM text generation speed dropping to a poor 2.44 tokens/sec. However, small model text generation is top-tier at 390.7 tokens/sec. Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, this server is designed for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, software compilation, and static web serving.
